title: War Scroll (1QM) — Hobah Research Reading
about: The War Scroll (1QM), from Qumran Cave 1, describes an eschatological conflict between the Sons of Light and the forces of darkness. Nineteen columns are preserved to varying degrees. The work combines battle organization, trumpet and banner texts, priestly exhortation, prayer, and apocalyptic expectation.

translation.status: Hobah provisional research reading — not a line-by-line translation of 1QM
translation.base_text: The ancient Hebrew 1QM manuscript is the source framework, with its nineteen-column sequence used for orientation. The present English text is a Hobah thematic reader synthesis, not a diplomatic transcription or a critical reconstruction.
translation.method: New Hobah English prose presents the major recoverable content and sequence of 1QM without copying a modern copyrighted English translation. Explanatory sentences and thematic transitions are editorial Hobah prose and therefore are not represented as words of the manuscript. A future direct edition must be checked line by line against a documented Hebrew transcription and mark every damaged or reconstructed passage explicitly.
translation.confidence: Medium-high for the broad structure and themes; not yet rated for line-level equivalence to the Hebrew manuscript
translation.notes: Source-integrity correction: the earlier edition used exact column labels even though portions of the English are explanatory synopsis rather than direct translation. The sections are now reader labels. Cave 4 War Scroll material must remain separate unless a future edition explicitly identifies a parallel witness.
translation.license_note: The ancient Hebrew manuscript text is public domain. Hobah English prose is newly prepared for this project. Modern copyrighted critical reconstructions or translations may be consulted for scholarship but are not copied into production wording.
translation.completeness: nineteen-part research reading of the surviving work; not a diplomatic or complete critical edition

chapters.label: Reading I — The final war
chapters.text: The first attack of the Sons of Light shall be made against the lot of the Sons of Darkness, against the army of Belial: the troops of Edom, Moab, the sons of Ammon, the Philistines, the Kittim of Asshur, and those who help them from among the violators of the covenant. The sons of Levi, Judah, and Benjamin, together with the exiles of the wilderness, shall fight them. The battle will be severe, for the powers of light and darkness will contend according to the mysteries of God. In the appointed campaigns the advantage will pass back and forth, but in the final lot the mighty hand of God will humble Belial and all the spirits of his dominion.

chapters.label: Reading II — Years and campaigns
chapters.text: The war is ordered by appointed times. Years of preparation, release, and battle are distinguished, and the tribes are mustered for service according to age and strength. The army shall not rush into conflict without order, for the war belongs to God and its times are fixed. The congregation shall count its campaigns and rest periods, keeping the holy seasons even in the years of battle.

chapters.label: Reading III — Trumpets of assembly
chapters.text: Trumpets shall bear inscriptions for the summons of the congregation, the chiefs, the camps, and the fighting formations. Other trumpets announce the opening of battle, pursuit, ambush, withdrawal, and return. When the priests sound them, the people shall know the command without confusion. The sound is not merely military: the trumpets proclaim that remembrance before God accompanies the host of Israel.

chapters.label: Reading IV — Standards and banners
chapters.text: The standards of the whole congregation, the tribes, the divisions, the thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens shall be marked according to their companies. Names of God, words of truth, and declarations of his majesty are associated with the banners. Each formation shall remain in its place, so that the army is one ordered assembly rather than a crowd driven by fear.

chapters.label: Reading V — Weapons and shields
chapters.text: The warriors shall prepare shields, spears, javelins, swords, and the equipment assigned to each rank. The shields and weapons bear signs and words recalling God's power and the appointed vengeance against wickedness. The text measures equipment and formations in detail, presenting the battle line as disciplined and consecrated rather than improvised.

chapters.label: Reading VI — The battle line
chapters.text: The infantry shall advance by ordered ranks, with men appointed for throwing weapons, men carrying long spears, and men prepared for close fighting. Spaces are kept between the formations so that one line may move without breaking another. Officers stand with their units, and the signals of trumpets and standards govern every advance and turn.

chapters.label: Reading VII — Holiness of the camp
chapters.text: The camp of battle shall be kept holy because the holy angels accompany the host. Anyone disqualified by grave bodily impurity shall not enter the fighting assembly until restored according to the rule. Filth, indecency, and careless conduct are forbidden within the camp. The people are to remember that the presence of God, not numerical strength, is their confidence.

chapters.label: Reading VIII — Priests before the ranks
chapters.text: Before the battle the priests shall go out between the lines in sacred garments. They shall strengthen the hearts of the warriors and sound the appointed trumpets. The officers shall arrange the companies, and when the signal is given the battle line shall move forward in measured order. No one is to leave his station through panic, because the priests declare that God himself stands with his people.

chapters.label: Reading IX — Cavalry and pursuit
chapters.text: Mounted troops and reserve companies are assigned their place beside the infantry. Some are appointed to encircle, some to pursue, and some to support a line under pressure. The rule distinguishes horses and riders suitable for service and warns against disorder in pursuit. Victory must not become undisciplined violence; every movement remains subject to the signals and the appointed commanders.

chapters.label: Reading X — Remember the ancient victories
chapters.text: The congregation shall recall the deeds by which God rescued Israel in earlier generations. He broke mighty kings, delivered the weak from the strong, and made the boast of armies collapse. Therefore the warriors are told not to trust bow, sword, horse, or human arm. Their strength is the God who chose Israel and who judges the arrogant nations.

chapters.label: Reading XI — Priestly exhortation
chapters.text: The chief priest shall say to those arrayed for battle: ‘Be strong and do not fear them. Their heart is for emptiness and their strength passes away, but the God of Israel is with us. He has appointed a day of battle against every spirit of wickedness. Remember that he saved our fathers when there was no human power to save them. Today the battle is his.’ The people shall answer with courage and remain in their ranks.

chapters.label: Reading XII — The heavenly host
chapters.text: The earthly battle is described as joined to a heavenly one. The holy ones and the angelic host stand in God's lot, while the spirits of Belial strengthen the lot of darkness. The congregation blesses the God of gods who raises the lowly and brings down the proud. His kingdom is everlasting, and the dominion of wickedness has an appointed end.

chapters.label: Reading XIII — Curse on Belial
chapters.text: The priests and Levites pronounce judgment on Belial and the spirits of his lot: may their counsel be darkness, their strength confusion, and their dominion brought to nothing. The congregation blesses the God of Israel for his truth and asks that deceit be removed from the earth. The language of curse is directed toward the apocalyptic enemies of the covenant and the spiritual power understood to stand behind them.

chapters.label: Reading XIV — Thanksgiving after deliverance
chapters.text: After a successful engagement the people shall gather and bless God for preserving the remnant of his people. They confess that victory did not come from their own arm. He gave courage to the faint, steadied the trembling knee, and delivered the enemy into judgment. The slain and the danger of battle are not hidden; thanksgiving is offered because life and rescue are understood to come from God.

chapters.label: Reading XV — The decisive engagement
chapters.text: When the decisive battle approaches, the formations are arranged again and the priests take their places. The host is warned that the testing will be severe. Belial's power is permitted a final moment within the appointed mystery, so the Sons of Light must not interpret danger as abandonment. The command is to hold the line until God's appointed help appears.

chapters.label: Reading XVI — When the line falters
chapters.text: In the crisis of battle some of the Sons of Light fall, and fear enters the ranks. Then the priests sound the trumpets of remembrance and call the warriors back to courage. ‘The trial is from God, and he has not forgotten his covenant. Stand firm, for the end of the dominion of wickedness is fixed.’ The companies reform and prepare to return against the enemy.

chapters.label: Reading XVII — God's intervention
chapters.text: At the appointed moment God acts against the army of Belial. The text pictures heavenly and earthly power converging in judgment. The courage of the wicked fails, their formations are broken, and those who had trusted in violence are thrown into confusion. Israel's victory is celebrated as the work of the mighty God and the help of his holy host rather than the achievement of superior weapons.

chapters.label: Reading XVIII — Pursuit of the defeated host
chapters.text: The defeated forces are pursued according to the commands of the officers and the signals of the trumpets. The victorious companies are still bound by order and holiness. The scroll's concern remains larger than ordinary warfare: the pursuit symbolizes the removal of the lot of darkness and the vindication of those who held to the covenant.

chapters.label: Reading XIX — Final blessing
chapters.text: The surviving conclusion gives praise to the God who has destroyed the dominion of wickedness and magnified his name among his people. The congregation blesses him for the appointed victory, for the help of the holy ones, and for the overthrow of Belial's lot. [The final lines are damaged.] The scroll closes in the atmosphere of triumph, purification, and the expectation that God's rule will be openly established.
